clue.text: Doris cavorting by couch, undressed

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about wildly, so the name Doris is jumbled

parts.note: a couch is a piece of furniture to lie on, a bed

explanation.surface: Someone called Doris dances about beside a sofa, having taken her clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' makes DISRO from the letters of Doris.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrobe is to take one's clothes off, so a disrobed person has been stripped.

clue.text: Scotsman outside wicked African city

indicators.note: outside means the Scotsman's name goes round the word for wicked

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name
bad means wicked or evil

explanation.surface: A Scotsman standing outside a sinful city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-west Nigeria.

clue.text: One sort of music or another introducing Georgia

indicators.note: introducing means the music comes first and leads into the state

parts.note: another sort of music, rag, as in ragtime
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A musical genre, or a different one, brought in by a singer from Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a form of dance music derived from reggae and dancehall.

clue.text: A boy gone mad having received very encouraging message before journey

indicators.note: having received means the jumbled letters take in the letter for very
mad suggests crazed and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazed lad gets a very cheering message before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges A BOY GONE, and V goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon voyage is French for 'good journey', a farewell wish to a traveller.

clue.text: Philosopher performed, having rushed up

parts.note: did means performed or carried out

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for rushed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tore means rushed or raced

explanation.surface: A thinker did something, having hurried upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was an eighteenth-century French philosopher who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Office worker is pretty stupid, about to be sacked

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled, so the letters of 'is pretty' are rearranged
sacked means dismissed, so the letters for 'about' are thrown out of the mix

parts.note: RE is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A secretary is described as rather dim and on the verge of being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is pretty' has the letters of the answer plus RE ('about'); 'to be sacked' throws RE out, and 'stupid' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist is a clerical employee who types documents, a classic office job.

clue.text: Made an effort, being weary, a bit confused inside

indicators.note: a little muddle among the middle letters of the word for weary

parts.note: tired means weary

explanation.surface: Someone, though exhausted and slightly muddled, tried hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit confused inside' swaps the middle I and R of TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To try is to make an attempt, so tried means attempted, made an effort.

clue.text: Favourite uncle somehow hiding a bad temper

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: hiding means the jumbled letters conceal the A inside them
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of uncle are scrambled

explanation.surface: A beloved uncle covering up a grumpy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes ULNCE from UNCLE; 'hiding' tucks A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky irritability, a peevish or childish ill temper.

clue.text: Loner thus wanting literature, a couple of lines?

parts.note: so means thus or in this way
RY is short for railway, whose track is a pair of lines

explanation.surface: A recluse who longs for reading, perhaps just a few lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is only a link: it means desiring, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary is a recluse, a person who lives alone.

clue.text: Limit damage produced by drink

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A warning that harm comes from alcohol up to a certain point.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an edge or boundary, the limit of a page or area.

clue.text: Set of books this writer wrapped in paper in tasteful style

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so the books and the writer go inside the paper

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
this writer is the setter, who refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A writer's books arrive neatly wrapped in newspaper, presented with taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Daintily means delicately and with refinement, which is doing something in a tasteful manner.

clue.text: Lover makes soldier lament no end

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: no end means the last letter of the word for lament is dropped

parts.note: to mourn is to lament

explanation.surface: A romance in which a soldier gives his sweetheart endless grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' takes the last letter off MOURN to leave MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit or secret romantic partner, a lover.

clue.text: Thin little girl with musical instrument

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
a lute is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A slender young girl carrying a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute is to thin a liquid by adding water, so the verb sense of thin fits.

clue.text: Left in desolate place with little money, engineers building for community

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for the desolate place

parts.note: a heath is open, uncultivated land, a bleak place
a cent is a coin of small value
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Engineers abandoned in a wilderness with hardly any cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A health centre is a building where a local population sees doctors and nurses, serving the community.

clue.text: Yobs lashing out about nothing repeatedly

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the zeros
out in the sense of wild or out of order, so the letters of lashing are rearranged
repeatedly means the letter for nothing appears twice

parts.note: O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Thugs lashing out violently over nothing, time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lashing out' reads as one phrase in the surface, but 'out' is the anagram signal, making HLIGANS (split H/LIGANS) that 'about' wraps round the zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobs is British slang for loutish young men, which hooligans are.

clue.text: Set against a ledge, wobbling

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: wobbling means shaking unsteadily, so the letters of 'a ledge' are reordered

explanation.surface: Something placed against a shelf that is unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: Set as in a jelly that has set: congealed means thickened into a solid.

clue.text: Oil's nice possibly as a sort of lubricant

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Oil is pleasant, perhaps, as a kind of lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone is a synthetic polymer used in greases and oils for lubrication.

clue.text: Nasty ice on side bed — problem in the earliest garden?

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty patch of ice beside a flower bed causes a problem in an old garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The earliest garden is Eden, where Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit against God's command.
explanation.definitionFit: Defying God's order not to eat from the tree was the original sin in Eden, a refusal to obey.

clue.text: Designs inside temporary accommodation

parts.note: in means inside
tents are shelters put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Plans drawn up within a campsite of makeshift lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs in the sense of purposes or aims: intents are intentions.

clue.text: A line of language?

parts.note: seems to ask for a family of tongues, but means a short dash used in writing to join words

explanation.surface: A question about a family or lineage of tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is a short horizontal stroke linking parts of compound words.

clue.text: Getting rid of top motorsport group

parts.note: Formula One, F1, is the top level of motor racing; the figure 1 is read as the letter I
a ring is a group of people, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the leading motor-racing organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing an employee is dismissing them, getting rid of them.

clue.text: Beef good and ready to eat

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Quality meat that is ready for the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and gripe are both informal words for a complaint.

clue.text: Periodic times making us sad yet resolved

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down and reworked, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Recurring occasions that leave us unhappy, though we are still determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuesdays come round once every week, so they are times recurring at regular intervals.

clue.text: Dope beginning to disturb a stomach

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of disturb is taken

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A drug that starts to upset the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information, and a datum is a single piece of information.

clue.text: Giving party attended by group of people

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a nation is a people sharing a country

explanation.surface: A party attended by a crowd, at which presents are given.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, the act or thing of giving to a cause.

clue.text: Tree illuminated, one at back of church

indicators.note: at back of means the numeral comes after the abbreviation for church

parts.note: lit means lit up, illuminated
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A tree lit up, standing alone behind a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, or lychee, is a Chinese fruit tree.

clue.text: The Parisian coming to Chichester maybe as a tenant

parts.note: les is the French plural for the, as used in Paris
Chichester is an example of a see, the diocese of a bishop

explanation.surface: A French person moves into the English town of Chichester, renting a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Chichester is a cathedral city in West Sussex, England, seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a property under a lease, which makes them a tenant.

clue.text: Grounds under water?

parts.note: coffee grounds settle at the bottom of a cup of liquid; matter that sinks to the bed of water is this deposit

explanation.surface: Pitches or land flooded beneath water.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter, like dregs or silt, that settles to the bottom of a liquid.
